title: Purity for a finite separable normalization over a regular domain
statement:
Let $A$ be a regular Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-regular-scheme], let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, and let $L/K$ be a finite separable field extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Put $C=\overline A^{\,L}=\{z\in L:z\text{ is integral over }A\}$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], and suppose $C$ is finite as an $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ of height one (nonzero, with no prime strictly between $(0)$ and $\mathfrak p$), and every prime $\mathfrak q\subset C$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$, assume that the module of relative Kahler differentials is zero:
$$\Omega_{C_{\mathfrak q}/A_{\mathfrak p}}=0$$
[def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Then $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is finite etale [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. No excellence, completeness, or henselian hypothesis on $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BMB (pione-lemma-purity, Purity of branch locus): applied to the finite dominant normalization in a finite separable field extension; localization and going down give equality of the local dimensions. The dimension-zero case is a finite separable field extension.

proof.text: Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be the structural map. Module finiteness makes $f$ finite, hence quasi-finite (in particular locally of finite type). The finite-algebra Noetherian lemma makes $C$ Noetherian, so $X,Y$ are locally Noetherian. The integral-closure lemma makes $C$ a normal domain with fraction field $L$; its prime localizations are normal domains. Regularity makes $A$ a normal ring; since $A$ is a domain, local normality makes it an integrally closed domain. Every $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular local by the hypothesis on $A$.

For any prime $\mathfrak q\subset C$, set $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$. Then $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q=\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p$. Indeed, $A\subset C$ is integral by the definition of $C$. Incomparability sends each strict chain of primes ending at $\mathfrak q$ to a strict chain ending at $\mathfrak p$, giving one inequality of heights. Conversely, start a chain ending at $\mathfrak p$ with the chosen prime $\mathfrak q$ above its last term, and repeatedly apply going down to lift its terms backwards. Distinct contractions force distinct lifted terms, giving the reverse inequality. Chains not ending at the chosen prime can be enlarged by it. The dimension-of-localization lemma identifies these heights with $\dim C_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\dim A_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Tags 00H8 (proposition-going-down-normal-integral), 00GT (lemma-integral-no-inclusion); height comparison written out by lifting and contracting chains, as used in pione-lemma-purity.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q'$ have height one in $C$. The preceding comparison shows that $\mathfrak p'=\mathfrak q'\cap A$ has height one. The hypothesis therefore gives $\Omega_{C_{\mathfrak q'}/A_{\mathfrak p'}}=0$. The formal-unramifiedness criterion makes the local ring map $A_{\mathfrak p'}\to C_{\mathfrak q'}$ formally unramified. Apply the stalk-neighbourhood lemma to the locally finite type $f$: it gives an open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak q'$ on which $f$ is formally unramified. A formally unramified morphism locally of finite type is unramified, so $f$ is unramified at $\mathfrak q'$. This treats every height-one point of $X$, hence every height-one generalization required by local purity.

source.place: Tag 02GF (lemma-unramified-at-point), with Algebra Tag 00UO (lemma-characterize-formally-unramified) and More on Morphisms Tag 02HE for locally finite type formal unramifiedness.

proof.text: The generic point also has an etale source neighbourhood. Finite module generators generate $C$ as an $A$-algebra, so the Noetherian finite-type lemma makes $C$ finitely presented over $A$. At $(0)\subset C$, its stalk is $L$ and the base stalk is $K$; these are the fraction fields from the hypotheses and Step 1. The $K$-module $L$ is flat and $\Omega_{L/K}=0$ by separability. By localization of differentials, $(\Omega_{C/A})_{(0)}\cong\Omega_{L/A}$. An $A$-derivation of $L$ kills $K$: it kills $a/b$ for $a,b\in A$, $b\ne0$, since $D(b^{-1})=-b^{-2}D(b)=0$. Thus the universal properties identify $\Omega_{L/A}=\Omega_{L/K}=0$. The etale-at-a-prime criterion now gives an etale neighbourhood of $(0)$.

source.place: Tags 00FP (lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation), 00RT (lemma-differentials-localize), 090W (lemma-characterize-separable-algebraic-field-extensions), 08WD (lemma-etale-flat-unramified-finite-presentation); the equality of A- and K-derivations is written explicitly.

proof.text: Finally fix a nonzero prime $\mathfrak q\subset C$ and let $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$. Since $C$ is a domain, $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ shows that its height is at least one. Step 2 gives equality of the two local dimensions. Step 1 gives a normal source stalk, a regular target stalk, locally Noetherian schemes, and quasi-finiteness at this point. Step 3 gives unramifiedness at all its generalizations whose source local dimension is one. Local purity of branch locus therefore says that $f$ is etale at $\mathfrak q$. Together with Step 4 this gives etale neighbourhoods covering every point of $X$; the source-local definition of etaleness makes $f$ etale. Finiteness was already proved in Step 1, so $f$ is finite etale. This also covers the case that $A$ is a field: then Step 2 forces every prime of $C$ to have height zero and Step 4 is the only pointwise case.

Step 2: 00GT plus going down 00H8 (A normal domain, C a domain integral over A, A in C) give ht q = ht p for every q, via 00KF/00E3. Step 3: a height-one q' contracts to a height-one p', and 00UO, 02GF and 02HE give unramified at q', as hypothesis (5) needs. Step 4: 00FP gives finite presentation, C_(0)=L, L is flat over K, Omega_{L/A}=Omega_{L/K} (the derivation argument checks), Omega_{L/K}=0, and 00U6 (3)=>(2) gives an etale neighbourhood. Step 5: nonzero q has height >=1, purity applies, the cover is local on the source, and finiteness comes from Step 1.
